channel.title: Chinese Room — AI project notes
channel.description: Joe Dowling’s notes on training networks, quantising language models and building agents.

item.title: AI, a Lego robot and a Rubik's cube
item.description: I trained a network to suggest cube moves, used search to find solutions, and sent them to a Lego robot. The best checkpoint solved 37 of 100 test cubes scrambled with 20 moves.

item.title: Removing a refusal direction from an open-weight model
item.description: I tested whether removing a direction from a model’s internal activations reduced refusal. On the reported set of 100 harmful prompts, refusals fell from 100 to 6.

item.title: NVFP4 quantisation of Mixtral 8×7B
item.description: I quantised Mixtral on the DGX Spark. The weights got smaller, but software compatibility problems prevented inference tests of the quantised model.

item.title: Building a multi-agent workflow in Haskell
item.description: Three local models debate a topic through a Haskell program. The article covers message types, state and the host that introduced the wrong debate.
